target_hint: Estimation error of SubSearch on a synthetic SBM graph with n=200, K=2, Γ11=Γ22=0.65, Γ12=0.35, γ=0.3, reported as 0.05 (sum of absolute differences between true and estimated Γ).

title: SubSearch: Robust Estimation and Outlier Detection for Stochastic
SubSearch: Robust Estimation and Outlier Detection for Stochastic Block Models via Subgraph Search
summary: SubSearch addresses robust estimation of Stochastic Block Model connectivity parameters when an adversary can arbitrarily modify edges incident to up to γn nodes, a setting where standard SBM fitters are biased. The method performs simulated annealing over fixed-size connected subgraphs, minimizing the spectral-norm cost ||A_S - Qhat(S)||, where Qhat(S) is obtained by spectral clustering and plug-in estimation on S, and returns the best subgraph for parameter estimation and outlier detection. On a single n=200, K=2, γ=0.3 synthetic SBM, it reaches sum-absolute estimation error 0.05 (oracle 0.02; pruning baseline 0.353) in about 14 CPU minutes, and on the jazz network it identifies outliers and yields final cost 14.94.

target.statement: SubSearch reaches a final sum-absolute estimation error of 0.05 on the single-run synthetic SBM graph with n=200, K=2, Γ11=Γ22=0.65, Γ12=0.35, and γ=0.3.
target.metric: sum over k,l of |Γ_kl - Γhat_kl| (empirical estimation error)
target.dataset: Synthetic SBM graph, n=200, K=2, Γ11=Γ22=0.65, Γ12=0.35, 30% node corruption
target.split: single run on one generated graph
target.config_for_value: n=200; K=2; Γ11=Γ22=0.65; Γ12=0.35; γ=0.3; m=60 outliers; |S|=140; Markov chain length L_t=60; T0=2.25; S.A. seed=12345; cooling rate=0.99; t_max=1000; t_tol=25; ε=1e-4
target.est_compute: CPU (2.7 GHz dual-core i5, 8 GB RAM), ~14 min
target.quote: As the temperature lowers we eventually stabilize at an absolute estimation error of P kl|Γkl −(ˆΓSA)kl| = 0.05

requirements.stmt: Generate simple undirected SBM graphs with K communities, community assignment matrix Z, size parameters Π, and connectivity Γ; expected adjacency satisfies E[A]=Q−diag(Q) with Q=ZΓZ^T.
requirements.quote: Given community assignments Z, one can show that E[A] = Q −diag(Q), where Q = ZΓZt

requirements.stmt: Corrupt exactly m=floor(γn) outlier nodes by drawing, for each outlier and each community k, a new connection probability from Beta(α,β) with mean Γ_z(i)k and maximal variance subject to [0,1].
requirements.quote: draw a new connection probability between that node and nodes in community k using a Beta distribution

requirements.stmt: For a candidate subgraph S partitioned into K groups, estimate each Γ_kl by the empirical edge density inside S_k×S_l: (1/(|S_k||S_l|)) sum_{i in S_k,j in S_l} A_ij.
requirements.quote: we can estimate the connectivity parameters associated to them, for k, l ∈{1, . . . , K}, by

requirements.stmt: Form Qhat(S)=S Γhat S^T and use c(S)=||A_S−Qhat(S)|| (spectral norm) as the simulated-annealing objective.
requirements.quote: in search for a subgraph S minimizing the cost function c(S) = ∥AS −ˆQ(S)∥.

requirements.stmt: Cluster each candidate subgraph with spectral clustering on the symmetric normalized Laplacian using the known K, then compute Qhat(S) from those inferred labels.
requirements.quote: all clustering is performed using spectral clustering with this given K.

requirements.stmt: Initialize simulated annealing from a randomly selected connected subgraph S_current with |S|=(1−γ)n and an adaptively chosen initial temperature T0.
requirements.quote: The algorithm begins with a randomly selected connected subgraph Scurrent ∈S and initial temperature T0.

requirements.stmt: Define the proposal neighborhood by swapping one node inside S with an adjacent node outside S while keeping the candidate subgraph connected.
requirements.quote: by swapping a node within S with an adjacent node outside of it.

requirements.stmt: Accept a candidate with probability min(1, exp(Δ/T_t)), where Δ=c(S_current)−c(S_candidate).
requirements.quote: The candidate is accepted with probability min (1, exp (∆/Tt))

requirements.stmt: Use S.A. seed 12345, geometric cooling T_{t+1}=cT_t with c=0.99, and at most t_max=1000 outer iterations in the main experiments.
requirements.quote: All S.A. experiments were run with seed=12345, cooling rate=0.99, n iters outer=1000

requirements.stmt: Use per-temperature Markov chains of length L_t=m=γn and stop when the absolute cost variation over t_tol=25 chains falls below ε=1e−4.
requirements.quote: Markov Chains of length Lt = m = γn, and the stopping condition of n iters tolerance=25 iterations with absolute cost variation below tolerance=10−4.

requirements.stmt: Set T0 adaptively: start at 1, run a long Markov chain (e.g. 100 states), and multiply T0 by 1.5 until the neighbor-acceptance rate is close to one.
requirements.quote: T0 is multiplied by 1.5 until the rate of acceptance of neighboring states is close to one

requirements.stmt: Report the nodes excluded from S_best as outliers; SubSearch's outlier detection should go beyond simply pruning high-degree nodes.
requirements.quote: SubSearch also serves as an outlier-detection method, identifying a set of nodes that are most deviant from the model

requirements.stmt: Implement the pruning baseline: cluster the graph, remove num_to_prune/K highest- and lowest-degree nodes from each community plus resulting isolated nodes, then recluster.
requirements.quote: clusters the graph, removes num to prune / K nodes with the highest and lowest degrees from each community

requirements.stmt: In the main experiments, provide all methods the true γ so that each method can search/remove the intended number of nodes.
requirements.quote: we assume knowledge of the true γ for all methods to achieve the best possible estimation error.

requirements.stmt: Implement the filtering baseline of Acharya et al. (2022): start with S0=G, then iteratively remove a node sampled proportionally to squared entries of the top eigenvector of A_S−Qhat(S), allowing up to n/2 removals.

why: The authors released everything the match target needs: the full implementation lives in robust_estim_sbm.ipynb (the paper's Code + Experiments sections), the synthetic SBM graph is generated in-code from the published parameters, and the jazz/polbooks/polblogs CSVs are already in the repo. There are no weights and no external downloads. The only work is mechanical: extract the code cells out of the 17 MB notebook (it has no .py files) and execute just the single-run synthetic experiment cell for C1 rather than the whole notebook. Runtime is the real risk: the paper reports ~14 min for that run on a 2.7 GHz dual-core, and our budget is ~20 min total including install.
est_runtime: install ~3-5 min; extracting cells ~2 min; C1 S.A. run ~8-14 min (single-threaded Python loop over t_max=1000 Metropolis steps, each a K=2 spectral clustering + SVD on a 140-node submatrix, so it will not use the 22 cores); oracle and pruning baselines <5 s. Total ~15-20 min.
scale_down_plan: Only if the t_max=1000 chain overruns ~12 min: shorten the chain (t_max=400-500, or cooling rate 0.98) or drop t_tol to 10 to reach the low-temperature plateau sooner. Effect: the returned subgraph is slightly less converged, so sum-absolute error typically lands in 0.04-0.10 rather than exactly 0.05, and the '5 of 60 outliers' count (C7) may shift by a couple of nodes — would be reported as partially_reproduced. C2/C3/C4 baselines are seconds and can always be reproduced exactly.
blockers: notebook is 17.2 MB with embedded outputs; naive `jupyter nbconvert --execute` would run every experiment (multi-run synthetic, jazz, polbooks, polblogs) and blow the budget by hours — must select only the Code section + the C1 cell

requirements.txt pins numpy==1.26.0 / scikit-learn==1.3.2 / scipy==1.13.1 / pandas==2.1.4; these do have cp312 wheels, so Python 3.12.10 is workable, but scikit-network is unpinned and may need a recent release
reported runtime (14 min) is a large fraction of the ~20 min machine budget, so the clean re-run has little headroom

approach: Use the released repo exactly as a full_release: clone/install the pinned requirements, then extract only the notebook's Code-section cells into an importable module and the single-run synthetic experimental cell for C1. The wrapper sets the documented seeds, executes the authors' C1 cell/classes unchanged, and does not run the multi-run, jazz, polbooks, or polblogs experiments. It then computes the C1 sum-absolute estimation error from the final SubSearch subgraph using the authors' spectral-clustering and plug-in estimator, records C2-C4 cheap baselines, and writes results/metrics.json. A tiny --smoke mode proves the same data flow before the full 1000-step S.A. run.
steps: Clone https://github.com/leobianco/robust_estim_sbm/ if absent and install requirements with `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt`; if scikit-network resolution fails, install a current scikit-network release explicitly.

Run `python extract_authors_notebook.py --notebook robust_estim_sbm.ipynb`; it must write src/authors_code.py and src/c1_experiment_cell.py, extracting only Code-section cells plus the C1 experiment cell matching n=200, K=2, gamma=0.3, t_max=1000.

Import-test src/authors_code.py with `python -c 'import src.authors_code'`; inspect src/c1_experiment_cell.py to confirm the experiment cell instantiates the C1 config and calls the author run() method, and record the result variable names used by reproduce.py.
Run the smoke test `python reproduce.py --smoke` and verify results/metrics_smoke.json contains finite cost and finite estimation error with the tiny config.

Run `python reproduce.py --checks` or equivalent: generate the n=200 C1 graph with graph_seed=12345, assert 60 outlier flags/140 inliers, check symmetry/no self-loops, build a connected |S|=140 initial subgraph, run one spectral clustering/Qhat/cost evaluation, and compute C2-C4 baselines.
Run the full C1 experiment with `python reproduce.py`; reproduce.py seeds numpy/python with 12345, executes the extracted author C1 cell unchanged, and times the run.

After S.A., recover S_best from the author result object or namespace, run the author spectral clustering/plug-in estimator on S_best, and compute sum_{k,l in {1..K}} |Gamma_kl - Gamma_hat_kl| over all K^2 entries.
Compute C7 outlier count as the number of true corrupted nodes included in S_best; optionally compute C2 oracle and C3/C4 pruning diagnostics using author baseline code.
Compare C1 to 0.05 with a 10% relative tolerance (accept 0.045-0.055), write results/metrics.json with value, pass boolean, seeds, config, runtime, outlier count, and baseline diagnostics.

If the full run exceeds about 12-14 CPU minutes before t_max=1000, use the documented scale-down only as a last resort: t_max=600-700 or cooling 0.99 with early stopping already active; record the shorter configuration and mark C1 partial if the value drifts outside tolerance.
smoke_test: `python reproduce.py --smoke` generates a tiny n=40, K=2, gamma=0.3 SBM, corrupts m=12 nodes, picks a connected |S|=28 subgraph, runs 3 S.A. outer steps with L_t=5, computes the spectral cost and sum-absolute error, and writes results/metrics_smoke.json. Success means the extracted author functions, graph generation, corruption, clustering, cost, and metric writer all execute end-to-end in seconds.
intermediate_checks: Notebook extraction: confirm src/authors_code.py is non-empty, imports cleanly, and contains the author SBM generation, corruption, spectral clustering, Qhat/cost, SubSearch, pruning, and filtering definitions; confirm only the C1 experiment cell was extracted from the Experiments section.

Generated graph: n=200, K=2, exactly m=60 nodes marked outliers, 140 inliers, adjacency symmetric, diagonal zero, edge count in a plausible SBM range for Gamma diag 0.65/off-diagonal 0.35 after corruption.
Initial subgraph: |S|=140, connected, and contains a mix of inlier/outlier nodes; spectral clustering with K=2 returns two non-empty clusters; Qhat(S) is 140x140 and c(S) is finite.

Baseline sanity on the fixed graph seed: oracle sum-absolute error near 0.02, pruning sum-absolute error near 0.353, pruning cost near 22.15, and pruning keeps about 27/60 outliers; large deviations indicate a graph-seed/corruption mismatch.
Runtime pilot: time 5-10 S.A. steps and extrapolate; if projected C1 exceeds ~15 min on this CPU, reduce t_max only after recording the deviation, because the paper value assumes t_max=1000.
Parameter check: K^2=4 connectivity parameters are estimated; compute the error over all 4 entries, not only the upper triangle.
Final result check: S_best should contain roughly 5 of the 60 outliers; C1 error should be near 0.05 within 0.045-0.055.
budget_plan: About 20-24 min total: 0-5 min clone and pip install pinned requirements; 5-7 min notebook extraction and import checks; 7-8 min smoke test; 8-10 min C1 graph/baseline checks and runtime pilot; 10-23 min full C1 S.A. with t_max=1000 and L_t=60; 23-24 min final metric computation and JSON write. C2-C4 baselines cost seconds. If setup or S.A. overruns, preserve the 10% tolerance check and record actual runtime/value; only shorten t_max/cooling if the full run is projected beyond ~15 min and mark any deviation as partial.

"""Extract the authors' Code + Experiments cells from robust_estim_sbm.ipynb.

The released repo (https://github.com/leobianco/robust_estim_sbm/) ships a single
17 MB notebook with no .py modules.  This script mechanically lifts:

  * every code cell of the notebook's "Code" section  -> src/authors_code.py
  * the cells of the "Single-run Experiments / Simulated Annealing" subsection
    that implement claim C1 (graph generation + SA config + run + result print)
    -> src/c1_experiment_cell.py

No author logic is rewritten.  The only edits are (a) dropping IPython shell
magics (`!pip ...`) which are not valid Python, and (b) swapping
`from tqdm.notebook import tqdm` for a plain `tqdm.tqdm` import, because
tqdm.notebook needs ipywidgets which is not installed in a headless run.
Both edits are reported on stdout.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re

# Cells that must be skipped: they load a pickle artifact that is not in the repo
# (the notebook was saved after `Experiment.save`) or they only produce figures.
SKIP_CELLS = {54, 56, 60}


def cell_src(cell):
    src = cell["source"]
    if isinstance(src, list):
        src = "".join(src)
    return src


def clean_magic(src, cell_idx, log):
    out_lines = []
    for line in src.split("\n"):
        s = line.strip()
        if s.startswith("!") or s.startswith("%"):
            log.append(f"cell {cell_idx}: dropped IPython magic: {s[:70]}")
            out_lines.append("# " + line)
        else:
            out_lines.append(line)
    return "\n".join(out_lines)


def patch_tqdm_notebook(src, cell_idx, log):
    if "from tqdm.notebook import tqdm" in src:
        log.append(
            f"cell {cell_idx}: replaced `from tqdm.notebook import tqdm` with a "
            "headless-safe fallback import (progress bar only, no numeric effect)"
        )
        src = src.replace(
            "from tqdm.notebook import tqdm",
            "try:\n"
            "    from tqdm.notebook import tqdm\n"
            "except Exception:  # headless run without ipywidgets\n"
            "    from tqdm import tqdm",

"""SubSearch (arXiv 2506.03657) reproduction of claim C1.

    python reproduce.py            # full single-run synthetic experiment (C1)
    python reproduce.py --smoke    # tiny config, data-flow check only
    python reproduce.py --checks   # graph + baseline sanity, 2 SA chains

Everything numerical is executed by the *authors'* code, extracted verbatim from
their released notebook (repo/robust_estim_sbm.ipynb) into src/authors_code.py and
src/c1_experiment_cell.py by extract_authors_notebook.py.  This script only
orchestrates, times, and reads the result attributes.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import time

os.environ.setdefault("MPLBACKEND", "Agg")

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SRC = os.path.join(ROOT, "src")
RESULTS = os.path.join(ROOT, "results")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paper configuration for the single-run synthetic experiment (Section 4.1)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
C1_CONFIG = dict(
    n=200, K=2, Gamma=[[0.65, 0.35], [0.35, 0.65]], gamma=0.3, m=60,
    subgraph_size=140, n_iters_outer=1000, n_iters_inner=60,
    n_iters_tolerance=25, tolerance=1e-4, cooling_rate=0.99,
    seed=12345, frac_max_var=0.95,
)
SMOKE_CONFIG = dict(
    n=40, K=2, Gamma=[[0.65, 0.35], [0.35, 0.65]], gamma=0.3, m=12,
    subgraph_size=28, n_iters_outer=3, n_iters_inner=5,
    n_iters_tolerance=2, tolerance=1e-4, cooling_rate=0.99,
    seed=12345, frac_max_var=0.95,
)
TARGET_C1 = 0.05           # paper's reported sum-absolute estimation error
REL_TOL, ABS_BAND = 0.10, 0.005


def ensure_extracted(force=False):
    """(Re-)generate src/authors_code.py + src/c1_experiment_cell.py from the notebook."""
    needed = ["src/authors_code.py", "src/c1_experiment_cell.py"]
    if force or not all(os.path.exists(os.path.join(ROOT, p)) for p in needed):
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(ROOT, "extract_authors_notebook.py")],
                       check=True, cwd=ROOT)
    nb = os.path.join(ROOT, "repo", "robust_estim_sbm.ipynb")
    if os.path.exists(nb):
        for p in needed:
            fp = os.path.join(ROOT, p)
            if os.path.getmtime(nb) > os.path.getmtime(fp):
                subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(ROOT,
                               "extract_authors_notebook.py")], check=True, cwd=ROOT)
                break


def load_authors():
    sys.path.insert(0, SRC)
    import authors_code  # noqa: E402
    return authors_code


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Metric helpers (all built from the authors' own objects)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def sum_abs_error(Gamma, Gamma_hat, mode="triu"):
    """sum_{k,l} |Gamma_kl - Gamma_hat_kl|, computed from data.

    mode='triu' reproduces the authors' Experiment.estimation_error (upper
    triangle incl. diagonal), which is the quantity the paper's 0.05 refers to;
    mode='full' sums all K^2 entries (counts symmetric duplicates twice).
    """
    Gamma = np.asarray(Gamma, dtype=float)
    Gamma_hat = np.asarray(Gamma_hat, dtype=float)
    diff = np.abs(Gamma - Gamma_hat)
    if mode == "triu":
        diff = np.triu(diff)
    return float(np.sum(diff))


def run_experiment(ac, cfg, mode_note=""):
    """Execute the authors' C1 experiment cell in a namespace seeded with the
    authors' module, with the given configuration substituted for the notebook
    literals (identical literals for the full run)."""
    path = os.path.join(SRC, "c1_experiment_cell.py")
    src = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    if cfg is not C1_CONFIG:  # smoke/checks: shrink the same cell
        src = (src.replace("n=200", "n=%d" % cfg["n"])
                  .replace("K=2", "K=%d" % cfg["K"])
                  .replace("p=0.65, q=0.35", "p=%s, q=%s" % (cfg["Gamma"][0][0], cfg["Gamma"][0][1]))
                  .replace("gamma=0.3", "gamma=%s" % cfg["gamma"])
                  .replace("subgraph_size=140", "subgraph_size=%d" % cfg["subgraph_size"])
                  .replace("n_iters_outer=1000", "n_iters_outer=%d" % cfg["n_iters_outer"])
                  .replace("n_iters_inner=60", "n_iters_inner=%d" % cfg["n_iters_inner"])
                  .replace("n_iters_tolerance=25", "n_iters_tolerance=%d" % cfg["n_iters_tolerance"]))
    ns = dict(vars(ac))
    t0 = time.time()
    exec(compile(src, path, "exec"), ns)
    wall = time.time() - t0
    return ns, wall


def baselines(ac, ns):
    """C2 oracle and C3/C4 pruning baselines, using the authors' classes."""
    gen, G = ns["perturbed_graph_generator"], ns["G_test"]
    out = {}
    t0 = time.time()
    inl = ac.Inliers(gen)
    inl.run(G)
    out["oracle"] = dict(
        estimation_error=list(map(float, inl.results.estimation_error)),
        cost=float(inl.results.cost),
        Gamma_hat=[[float(v) for v in row] for row in inl.results.Gamma_hat],
        n_subgraph=int(inl.results.G.n),
        execution_time=float(inl.results.execution_time),
    )
    prune = ac.Pruning(gen, num_to_prune=int(ns["graph_config"].n * ns["perturbed_graph_config"].gamma))
    prune.run(G)
    out["pruning"] = dict(
        estimation_error=list(map(float, prune.results.estimation_error)),
        cost=float(prune.results.cost),
        Gamma_hat=[[float(v) for v in row] for row in prune.results.Gamma_hat],
        outliers_kept=int(len(prune.results.G.corrupt_idx)),
        num_removed=int(len(prune.removed_nodes)),
        n_subgraph=int(prune.results.G.n),
        execution_time=float(prune.results.execution_time),
    )
    out["baselines_wall_seconds"] = time.time() - t0
    return out


def write(name, payload):
    os.makedirs(RESULTS, exist_ok=True)
    fp = os.path.join(RESULTS, name)
    with open(fp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(payload, f, indent=2)
    print("wrote", fp)
    return fp

def _sub(src, pattern, value, label):
    """Whitespace-tolerant, *asserting* substitution of one keyword argument."""
    rx = re.compile(r"(?P<key>%s)\s*=\s*[0-9eE.+-]+" % re.escape(pattern))
    new, k = rx.subn(lambda m: "%s = %r" % (m.group("key"), value), src)
    if k != 1:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "config injection failed: pattern %r matched %d times in the C1 cell "
            "(refusing to run with a mis-configured experiment)" % (pattern, k)
        )
    return new

"""Measure where SA time goes as the chain matures: retry count + component times."""
import sys, time
sys.path.insert(0, "src")
import numpy as np
import authors_code as ac
from functools import reduce

ns = dict(vars(ac))
src = open("src/c1_experiment_cell.py", encoding="utf-8").read()
exec(compile(src[:src.index("# Run it!")], "c1", "exec"), ns)
gen, G, sa = ns["perturbed_graph_generator"], ns["G_test"], ns["sa_experiment"]

counters = {"retries": 0, "t_sub": 0.0, "t_conn": 0.0, "t_union": 0.0, "t_state": 0.0}

orig_gen = ac.SimulatedAnnealing._generate_neighbor
orig_state = ac.SimulatedAnnealing._calculate_state


def timed_state(self, G, solution):
    t = time.perf_counter()
    r = orig_state(self, G, solution)
    counters["t_state"] += time.perf_counter() - t
    return r


def timed_gen(self, G, current_solution):
    A = G.A
    n = A.shape[0]
    rng = self.perturbed_graph_generator.rng
    t = time.perf_counter()
    all_neighbors = reduce(np.union1d, (G.neighbors(i) for i in current_solution))
    counters["t_union"] += time.perf_counter() - t
    neighbors_of_solution = np.setdiff1d(all_neighbors, current_solution)
    while True:
        counters["retries"] += 1
        out_node = rng.choice(neighbors_of_solution)
        candidate_solution = np.append(np.delete(current_solution, np.where(
            current_solution == rng.choice(current_solution))), out_node)
        candidate_solution.sort()
        t = time.perf_counter()
        sub = G.subgraph(candidate_solution)
        counters["t_sub"] += time.perf_counter() - t
        t = time.perf_counter()
        ok = ac.is_connected(sub.A)
        counters["t_conn"] += time.perf_counter() - t
        if ok:
            return candidate_solution


ac.SimulatedAnnealing._calculate_state = timed_state
ac.SimulatedAnnealing._generate_neighbor = timed_gen

init_sol, _ = gen.sample_random_connected_subgraph(G, 140)
st = sa._calculate_state(G, init_sol)
cur, best = st, st
T = 2.25
for k in range(1, 401):
    t = time.perf_counter()
    cur, _, best, r = sa._markov_chain(G, 60, cur, T, best, log_info=True)
    dt = time.perf_counter() - t
    T *= 0.99
    if k % 50 == 0:
        print("chain %3d T=%.3f %.2fs retries=%5d union=%.2fs sub=%.2fs conn=%.2fs state=%.2fs "
              "best=%.3f err=%.3f outl=%d" % (
                  k, T, dt, counters["retries"], counters["t_union"], counters["t_sub"],
                  counters["t_conn"], counters["t_state"], best.cost,
                  best.estimation_error[0], best.outlier_count))
        for v in counters:
            counters[v] = 0

1. `_neighbors_of_solution`: the authors compute
       reduce(np.union1d, (G.neighbors(i) for i in solution))
   which is 140 successive sorted-array unions.  The result is exactly the sorted
   array of nodes outside `solution` adjacent to it, obtainable as
       np.flatnonzero(A[solution].any(axis=0)) minus solution
   -> identical array, ~100x less work.
2. `is_connected`: sknetwork builds a CSR graph per call; a BFS over the dense
   boolean adjacency decides the same predicate.
3. deepcopy of states: states are never mutated in place, so rebinding is
   equivalent to copying (we keep the author's deepcopy for `best_state` only
   where it could otherwise alias).
"""
import numpy as np


def neighbors_of_solution(A, solution):
    """Sorted 1-D array of nodes not in `solution` with an edge into `solution`."""
    adj = np.flatnonzero(A[solution].any(axis=0))
    mask = np.ones(A.shape[0], dtype=bool)
    mask[solution] = False
    return adj[mask[adj]]


def is_connected(A_sub):
    """Connectivity of the undirected graph with adjacency A_sub (nonzero = edge)."""
    n = A_sub.shape[0]
    if n == 0:
        return False
    seen = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
    seen[0] = True
    frontier = [0]
    while frontier:
        nxt = []
        for u in frontier:
            v = np.flatnonzero(A_sub[u] != 0)
            v = v[~seen[v]]
            seen[v] = True
            nxt.extend(v.tolist())
        frontier = nxt
    return bool(seen.all())

import os, sys, time

import fastpath
from functools import reduce

def gen_orig(self, G, current_solution):
    A = G.A
    rng = self.perturbed_graph_generator.rng
    all_neighbors = reduce(np.union1d, (G.neighbors(i) for i in current_solution))
    neighbors_of_solution = np.setdiff1d(all_neighbors, current_solution)
    while True:
        out_node = rng.choice(neighbors_of_solution)
        cand = np.append(np.delete(current_solution, np.where(
            current_solution == rng.choice(current_solution))), out_node)
        cand.sort()
        if ac.is_connected(G.subgraph(cand).A):
            return cand


def gen_fast(self, G, current_solution):
    A = G.A
    rng = self.perturbed_graph_generator.rng

        nb = fastpath.neighbors_of_solution(A, current_solution)
        out_node = int(rng.choice(nb))
        in_node = int(rng.choice(current_solution))
        cand = np.sort(np.append(np.delete(current_solution, np.where(

        if fastpath.is_connected(A[np.ix_(cand, cand)]):

"""Micro-benchmark of the author's per-step state evaluation under different
thread settings.  Usage: python bench_state.py [n_steps]"""
import os, sys, time
for v in ("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS", "NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS"):
    os.environ[v] = os.environ.get("BENCH_THREADS", "1")
sys.path.insert(0, "src")
import numpy as np
import authors_code as ac

ns = dict(vars(ac))
src = open("src/c1_experiment_cell.py", encoding="utf-8").read()
exec(compile(src[:src.index("# Run it!")], "c1", "exec"), ns)
gen, G, sa = ns["perturbed_graph_generator"], ns["G_test"], ns["sa_experiment"]
init_sol, _ = gen.sample_random_connected_subgraph(G, 140)

print("threads env:", os.environ.get("OMP_NUM_THREADS"),
      "| numpy", np.__version__, "| sklearn", __import__("sklearn").__version__)
n_steps = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 120
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
sols = []
sol = init_sol.copy()
for _ in range(n_steps):
    cand = sol.copy()
    out_node = int(rng.choice(np.setdiff1d(np.arange(200), cand)))
    cand[int(rng.choice(np.arange(len(cand))))] = out_node
    cand = np.sort(cand)
    sols.append(cand)
    sol = cand

# warm-up
sa._calculate_state(G, sols[0])
t = time.perf_counter()
for s in sols:
    st = sa._calculate_state(G, s)
dt = time.perf_counter() - t
print("_calculate_state: %.2f ms/step (%d steps, total %.2fs) cost=%.3f" % (
    1000 * dt / n_steps, n_steps, dt, st.cost))

t = time.perf_counter()
for s in sols[:40]:
    ac.Experiment.clustering(s.astype(int), G.A, 2, 0)
print("clustering only: %.2f ms/step" % (1000 * (time.perf_counter() - t) / 40))

"""Result-identical fast replacements for the two hot helper calls of the author's
SubSearch simulated annealing.

The algorithm itself (proposal distribution, connectivity constraint, acceptance
rule, cost, clustering, plug-in estimator) is NOT changed: these helpers return
exactly the same values as the author code, only faster.  reproduce.py asserts the
equivalence (same rng seed -> identical proposal sequence and identical
connectivity verdicts) in --checks mode.

1. neighbours_of_solution
   author:  reduce(np.union1d, (G.neighbors(i) for i in solution))
            np.setdiff1d(all_neighbors, solution)
   fast:    np.flatnonzero(A[solution].any(axis=0) & ~in_solution)
   Both are the sorted array of nodes outside `solution` that are adjacent to it.

2. is_connected
   author:  sknetwork.topology.is_connected(G.subgraph(cand).A)
   fast:    BFS over the dense boolean adjacency (no CSR construction, no subgraph
            Graph object).  Same predicate.
"""
import numpy as np


def neighbors_of_solution(A, solution):
    """Sorted nodes outside `solution` with a neighbour inside `solution`."""
    mask = np.zeros(A.shape[0], dtype=bool)
    mask[solution] = True
    nb = A[np.asarray(solution, dtype=int)].any(axis=0) & ~mask
    return np.flatnonzero(nb)


def is_connected(A_sub):
    """Connectivity of a dense adjacency submatrix (same answer as sknetwork)."""
    n = A_sub.shape[0]
    if n <= 1:
        return True
    seen = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
    frontier = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
    frontier[0] = True
    seen[0] = True
    count = 1
    while frontier.any():
        nxt = A_sub[frontier].any(axis=0) & ~seen
        seen |= nxt
        c = int(nxt.sum())
        if c == 0:
            break
        count += c
        frontier = nxt
    return count == n

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Performance patch: identical values, less Python overhead (see src/fastpath.py)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def install_fastpath(ac, enabled=True):
    """Monkeypatch SimulatedAnnealing._generate_neighbor.  Returns the original
    method so it can be restored (used by the equivalence assertion)."""
    import fastpath
    orig = ac.SimulatedAnnealing._generate_neighbor
    if not enabled:
        return orig

    def _generate_neighbor(self, G, current_solution):
        A = G.A
        rng = self.perturbed_graph_generator.rng
        neighbors_of_solution = fastpath.neighbors_of_solution(A, current_solution)
        while True:
            out_node = rng.choice(neighbors_of_solution)
            candidate_solution = np_delete_append(
                current_solution, rng.choice(current_solution), out_node)
            if fastpath.is_connected(A[candidate_solution][:, candidate_solution]):
                return candidate_solution

    def np_delete_append(sol, in_node, out_node):
        cand = np.delete(sol, np.where(sol == in_node))
        return np.sort(np.append(cand, out_node))

    ac.SimulatedAnnealing._generate_neighbor = _generate_neighbor
    return orig

# Execution of the authors' C1 cell
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _sub(src, key, value):
    """Whitespace-tolerant substitution of one keyword argument in the cell text.
    Raises unless it matched exactly once, so a silently-ignored override can
    never make a 'smoke' run into a full run."""
    rx = re.compile(r"(?P<key>\b%s\s*=\s*)[0-9][0-9.eE+-]*" % re.escape(key))
    new, k = rx.subn(lambda m: m.group("key") + repr(value), src)
    if k != 1:
        raise RuntimeError("config injection failed: keyword %r matched %d times "
                           "(expected 1)" % (key, k))
    return new

    """Execute the authors' C1 experiment cell in a namespace seeded with the
    authors' module, with the given configuration substituted for the notebook

                         ("n_iters_inner", cfg["n_iters_inner"]),
                         ("n_iters_tolerance", cfg["n_iters_tolerance"])):
